content: Dipping tobacco, also referred to as American moist snuff or spit tobacco, is a type of smokeless tobacco product. It is commonly called dip, and the act of using it is known as dipping, having a dip, or packing a lip. Unlike chewing tobacco, which involves physically chewing the product, dipping tobacco is used by placing a small amount of tobacco between the lower or upper lip and the gums. The tobacco remains in contact with the inner lining of the mouth for approximately 20 to 30 minutes. During this time, nicotine is absorbed into the bloodstream via the inferior or superior labial arteries. The process of dipping often leads to the production of excess saliva, which users typically spit out. Swallowing this saliva can irritate the esophagus and may cause nausea or vomiting, although long-term users may develop a tolerance and experience no adverse effects from swallowing. Dipping tobacco is available in various cut sizes, which refer to the length and texture of the tobacco strands. The primary cut types include: Long Cut: Thin strands of tobacco, typically around 7 cm in length. Mid Cut: Small granules, approximately 1 cm³ in size. Fine Cut: Very small granules, slightly larger than grains of sand. Pouches: Finely cut tobacco wrapped in small, porous envelopes. The surface area of the tobacco plays a significant role in nicotine absorption. Finer cuts have a larger surface area, which facilitates greater nicotine absorption. Additionally, finer cuts tend to retain more moisture, which can further enhance nicotine delivery. Health Risks Associated with Dipping Tobacco Cancer Risks Dipping tobacco has been linked to several types of cancer, including oral cancer, esophageal cancer, and pancreatic cancer. While some researchers argue that smokeless tobacco may be less harmful than smoking due to fewer associated fatalities, it is not considered a safe alternative. Studies have shown that users of smokeless tobacco are exposed to higher levels of NNK, a potent carcinogen, compared to cigarette smokers. Cardiovascular Effects The impact of smokeless tobacco on cardiovascular health remains inconclusive. Some studies suggest that the cardiovascular risks associated with smokeless tobacco are lower than those linked to smoking but higher than those observed in non-users. For example, one study found that smokeless tobacco use has a modest effect on cardiovascular risk factors in young, physically fit men. However, a study conducted in Rajasthan, India, reported a significantly higher prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors—such as obesity, resting tachycardia, hypertension, high LDL cholesterol, low HDL cholesterol, and electrocardiographic changes—among tobacco users, whether they smoked or chewed tobacco, compared to non-users. These findings highlight the need for further research to clarify the cardiovascular risks of smokeless tobacco. Addiction Potential Dipping tobacco contains nicotine, which is the primary substance responsible for its addictive properties. While some Scandinavian and American smokeless tobacco products are considered to be at least 90% less hazardous than cigarette smoking, according to European Union policy, dipping tobacco remains highly addictive. Warning Labels In the United States, all tins of smokeless tobacco are required to display one of the following three warning labels on a rotating basis: WARNING: This product may cause mouth cancer. WARNING: This product may cause gum disease and tooth loss. WARNING: This product is not a safe alternative to smoking. Market and Industry As of the third quarter of 2006, UST Inc., a Connecticut-based company, held 62.5% of the market share for smokeless tobacco products. The company’s brands include Copenhagen, Skoal, Husky, and Red Seal. Other major players in the market include the Conwood subsidiary of Reynolds American Inc. and Swedish Match. In 2006, companies such as Altria Group Inc. (formerly Philip Morris Companies) and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company began test-marketing smokeless and spit-less tobacco products under the brand names Taboka and Camel Snus, respectively.
